subsystems.name: XNA monomers
subsystems.role: the alternative sugar or backbone units that replace DNA's deoxyribose and phosphate.

subsystems.name: Synthetic chemistry
subsystems.role: makes XNA strands of defined sequence in the lab.

subsystems.name: Engineered polymerases
subsystems.role: enzymes evolved to copy information between DNA and XNA.

subsystems.name: In vitro evolution system
subsystems.role: selects and amplifies XNA molecules with useful binding or catalytic activity.

subsystems.name: Characterisation tools
subsystems.role: read and confirm XNA sequences and structures.

buildSteps.title: Choose an XNA chemistry
buildSteps.detail: Pick a sugar or backbone that natural enzymes do not recognise, so the molecule is orthogonal to terrestrial biology.

buildSteps.title: Synthesise monomers and oligos
buildSteps.detail: Phosphoramidite monomers are made and linked on a solid support into XNA strands of defined length.

buildSteps.title: Evolve a polymerase
buildSteps.detail: Starting from a thermostable DNA polymerase, directed evolution selects variants that can copy DNA into XNA and XNA back into DNA.

buildSteps.title: Build a random library
buildSteps.detail: Millions of random XNA sequences are synthesised, each with a constant region for later amplification.

buildSteps.title: Run in vitro selection
buildSteps.detail: The library is exposed to a target; molecules that bind or catalyse are captured, copied back to DNA, amplified by PCR, and transcribed back to XNA for the next round.

buildSteps.title: Iterate with increasing stringency
buildSteps.detail: Repeated rounds enrich the best binders or catalysts, yielding XNA aptamers and XNAzymes.

buildSteps.title: Sequence and validate
buildSteps.detail: Selected molecules are cloned, sequenced via their DNA copies, and tested to confirm they fold and function as intended.

buildSteps.title: Test for heredity and evolution
buildSteps.detail: Show that the XNA can be copied with errors and that improved variants can be selected — the operational test of Darwinian evolution.

prerequisites.why: without custom monomers and solid-phase synthesis, no XNA strand can be made.
natural enzymes ignore XNA; polymerases must be evolved to read and write it.
provides the iterative selection that turns random XNA libraries into functional molecules.
XNA sequences are read indirectly through their DNA copies, so fast sequencing is essential.
true synthetic genetics requires XNA to be copied and mutated without help from natural biology.

pathway.milestone: lab demonstrations that XNA can store information and evolve in vitro
pathway.unlocks: proof that heredity is not unique to DNA and RNA.

pathway.milestone: polymerases with higher fidelity and broader XNA compatibility
pathway.unlocks: longer XNA genomes and more complex XNA catalysts.

pathway.milestone: orthogonal XNA systems that cannot interact with natural cells
XNA-based artificial life or life-detection tools for other planets
pathway.unlocks: a general understanding of the chemistry required for Darwinian evolution.
